key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that post-perovskite conducts lattice heat 44–55% better than bridgmanite at matched lower-mantle conditions.
engineering_relevance: The resulting conductivity parameterizations support lower-mantle thermal models, with Fe-free aggregate estimates of 9.5–11.4 W/(m K) at the core–mantle boundary.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine quasi-harmonic phase-boundary calculations with aggregate conductivity bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, otherwise identical transport calculations using MACE versus DFT forces differ in lattice conductivity by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: These intrinsic, Fe-free end-member estimates are a reference rather than a complete conductivity model for chemically complex mantle material.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
